# API

> Every endpoint of the Gripello API, as served by gripello.app.

> How to do things in Gripello, step by step.

# Account

> Sign up, sign in, password, two-factor, your data.

## Create an account

1. Open **Sign in** and tap **Create account**.
2. Enter first and last name, username, email and password.
3. Open the link in the email to verify your address.
4. Sign-up only shows when the operator allows it; otherwise ask your gym for an invitation.

<shot name="register" title="Create an account">



</shot>

## Sign in

1. Sign in with username or email and password, or with a passkey.
2. With two-factor on, enter the code from your authenticator app next.

<shot name="login" title="Sign in">



</shot>

## Reset your password

1. On the sign-in page tap **Reset password**.
2. Enter the email of your account and tap **Submit**.
3. Open the link in the email (valid 30 minutes) and choose a new password. All other sessions are signed out.

<shot name="reset" title="Reset your password">



</shot>

## Your account

1. Tap your name at the bottom of the menu.
2. Profile, friends, staff tools and the gyms you belong to.

<shot name="account" title="Your account">



</shot>

## Edit your profile and email

1. Open **Account → Settings → Profile**.
2. Change name, avatar or banner.
3. A new email address needs your password and is active once you open the confirmation link sent to it.

<shot name="settings-profile" title="Edit your profile and email">



</shot>

## Language and theme

1. **Settings → Preferences**: language, light/dark theme.

<shot name="settings-preferences" title="Language and theme">



</shot>

## Change your password

1. Open **Settings → Security**.
2. Enter the current and the new password, then save.

<shot name="settings-security" title="Change your password">



</shot>

## Turn on two-factor sign-in

1. **Settings → Security → Two-factor authentication**.
2. Set up an authenticator app or add a passkey.
3. Store the recovery codes somewhere safe.

## Sign out other devices

1. **Settings → Security** lists active sessions; sign out the ones you do not recognise.

## Download your data

1. **Settings → Security → Download your data → Email me a link**.
2. The link in the email works for 7 days.

## Delete your account

1. **Settings → Security → Delete account**.
2. Routes and reviews you created stay; your profile, logbook and memberships are removed.

## Notifications

1. **Settings → Notifications**: turn on push for this device and pick the topics.

<shot name="settings-notifications" title="Notifications">



</shot>

## Privacy

1. **Settings → Privacy**: who can follow you, leaderboard visibility, your name on reviews, sharing sends.

<shot name="settings-privacy" title="Privacy">



</shot>

## Activity log

1. **Account → Activity**: sign-ins and changes to your account.

<shot name="account-activity" title="Activity log">



</shot>


# Gym admin

> Staff, roles, map, settings, moderation.

## Invite staff

1. **Users → Invite member**.
2. Enter the email and pick a role; they get an invitation link.

<shot name="invite" title="Invite staff">



</shot>

## Roles and permissions

1. **Users → Roles & permissions**: create roles and tick what each may do.

<shot name="roles" title="Roles and permissions">



</shot>

## Draw the gym map

1. **Map editor**: pick a location, create the floor plan.
2. Draw walls, mats and the entrance; **Save**.

<shot name="admin-map" title="Draw the gym map">



</shot>

## Branding

1. **Settings → Branding**: app logo, browser icon, logo on route signs, cover image.

<shot name="admin-settings" title="Branding">



</shot>

## Grading scales

1. **Settings → Grading scales**: the scale for routes and for boulders.

<shot name="settings-grading" title="Grading scales">



</shot>

## TV screen

1. **Settings → TV screen**: what the gym TV shows.

<shot name="settings-tv" title="TV screen">



</shot>

## Gym TV

1. Open `/<gym>/tv` on a screen in the gym.

<shot name="tv" title="Gym TV">



</shot>

## Legal notice and privacy

1. **Settings → Legal notice** and **Privacy page** fill the gym pages below, or link your own.

<shot name="settings-legal" title="Legal notice and privacy">



</shot>

## Legal notice page

1. Public at `/<gym>/imprint`.

<shot name="imprint" title="Legal notice page">



</shot>

## Handle content reports

1. **Moderation**: reported reviews and content.
2. Hide or keep it; the reporter is notified (DSA).

<shot name="manage-moderation" title="Handle content reports">



</shot>

## Reviews

1. **Reviews**: read, filter and hide route reviews.

<shot name="manage-comments" title="Reviews">



</shot>


# Climbing

> Find routes, log ascents, follow friends.

## Find your gym

1. Open Gripello and search for your gym.
2. Open it; Gripello remembers it for next time.

<shot name="home" title="Find your gym">



</shot>

## See what is new

1. The gym overview shows new routes per wall, your progress and running competitions.

<shot name="overview" title="See what is new">



</shot>

## Find a route

1. Open **Routes**.
2. Filter by type, grade, colour, location or wall, or search by name, setter or grade.

<shot name="routes" title="Find a route">



</shot>

## Find routes on the map

1. Open **Map** and pick a hall.
2. Tap a wall to list its routes.

<shot name="map" title="Find routes on the map">



</shot>

## Scan a route sign

1. Tap the scan button or open **Scan**.
2. Point the camera at the QR code on the route sign; the route opens.

<shot name="scan" title="Scan a route sign">



</shot>

## Log an ascent

1. Open the route and tap **Log ascent**.
2. Pick Flash, Top or Attempt, the number of attempts and the date; add a private note if you like.
3. Save; the ascent lands in your logbook.

<shot name="tick" title="Log an ascent">



</shot>

## Rate and review a route

1. Open the route and tap **Write a review**.
2. Give stars, pick the grade it felt like, add a comment, **Submit**.

<shot name="review" title="Rate and review a route">



</shot>

## Report a problem with a route

1. Open the route, tap **⋯** and **Report a problem**.
2. Pick what is wrong (loose hold, missing tag …) and add details or a photo.
3. The setters get it as a task.

<shot name="defect" title="Report a problem with a route">



</shot>

## Keep a logbook

1. Open **Logbook**: sessions, timeline, stats, projects and badges.
2. Switch between boulders and routes and the time range at the top.

<shot name="logbook" title="Keep a logbook">



</shot>

## Follow friends

1. Open **Friends** and search for a climber.
2. Tap **Follow**; climbers who approve followers see a request first.

<shot name="friends" title="Follow friends">



</shot>

## Follow the feed

1. Open **Feed**: sends of the people you follow and new routes on walls you follow.

<shot name="feed" title="Follow the feed">



</shot>

## Climber profiles

1. Tap a climber anywhere to see their sends, stats and achievements.

<shot name="climber" title="Climber profiles">



</shot>

## Leaderboard

1. Open **Leaderboard** for the gym ranking; switch boulders/routes and the period.
2. Hide yourself in **Settings → Privacy**.

<shot name="leaderboard" title="Leaderboard">



</shot>

## Opening hours and contact

1. Open **Info** for opening hours, contact, facilities and address.

<shot name="info" title="Opening hours and contact">



</shot>


# Competitions

> Enter a competition or run one: categories, judging, live ranking.

## Find a competition

1. Open **Competitions** for upcoming, running and past events.

<shot name="competitions" title="Find a competition">



</shot>

## Enter a competition

1. Open it, fill in **Take part** and tap **Sign up**.
2. Log your attempts on your phone while it runs; the ranking updates live.

<shot name="competition" title="Enter a competition">



</shot>

## Rules

1. **Rules** explains scoring, categories and fair play for this event.

<shot name="competition-rules" title="Rules">



</shot>

## Create a competition

1. **Staff tools → Competitions → New competition**.
2. Pick discipline and scoring format, set the time, then add categories and boulders or routes.

<shot name="competition-new" title="Create a competition">



</shot>

## Run it

1. Move it through Draft → Registration open → Running → Ended → Results published.
2. **Participants**: check climbers in. **Export** the results.

<shot name="manage-competition" title="Run it">



</shot>

## Judge

1. **Judging**: pick a boulder, then count tries, zone and top per climber.

<shot name="manage-competition-judge" title="Judge">



</shot>

## Live ranking on a screen

1. Open **TV view** on a screen at the venue; it refreshes by itself.

<shot name="competition-tv" title="Live ranking on a screen">



</shot>


# Setting routes

> For setters: routes, signs, walls, inventory, defects.

## Staff tools

1. Tap **Staff tools** in the menu. What you see depends on your role.

<shot name="manage" title="Staff tools">



</shot>

## Add a route

1. **Manage routes → Create route**.
2. Set name, type, grade, anchor, location, setter, date and colour, then **Create**.
3. Put it on its wall under **Routes & resets** (below).

<shot name="route-create" title="Add a route">



</shot>

## Edit or archive routes

1. Tap the pencil to edit a route.
2. Select routes and **Archive** them when they come off the wall.
3. **Import routes** reads a spreadsheet.

<shot name="manage-routes" title="Edit or archive routes">



</shot>

## Print QR tags

1. **Manage routes**: select the routes, tap **Print**.
2. Pick language, layout and what to show, then **Export** a PDF; every tag carries the QR code climbers scan.

<shot name="print" title="Print QR tags">



</shot>

## Place routes on walls

1. **Routes & resets**: pick the hall.
2. Drag routes from the list onto a wall; **Save**.

<shot name="manage-map" title="Place routes on walls">



</shot>

## Take inventory

1. **Inventory**: choose a location and tap **Start scanning**.
2. Scan every route sign.
3. **Finish inventory** archives the routes that were not found.

<shot name="manage-inventory" title="Take inventory">



</shot>

## Fix defects

1. Problems climbers report land in **Tasks**.
2. Drag a task to In progress, Waiting or Done; the reporter is told when it is fixed.

<shot name="manage-tasks" title="Fix defects">



</shot>

## Plan work

1. **Tasks → New task**.
2. Pick Reset, Maintenance or Other, give it a title and priority, the location or wall, who does it and by when.

<shot name="task-new" title="Plan work">



</shot>

## Analytics

1. Routes set, reviews, stars, grade distribution and how long routes stay up.

<shot name="manage-analytics" title="Analytics">



</shot>


# Setup

> Self-host Gripello with Docker Compose.

## Setup Docker Compose

Running Gripello in production requires a commercial license, see [License](#license).

### Prerequisites

- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)
- [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/)

### Download Docker Compose File

```sh
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gripello/gripello/main/docker-compose.yml
```

### Docker Compose Configuration

The downloaded `docker-compose.yml` runs the app container and PostgreSQL. Set
`POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (e.g. in a `.env` file next to it) **before the first start**:
PostgreSQL only reads it when its volume is created.

```sh
echo "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24)" > .env
```

To pin the latest release instead of the rolling build, change the app image:

```yaml
services:
    gripello:
        image: ghcr.io/gripello/gripello:latest
```

### Running the Project

```sh
docker-compose up -d
```

## Getting Started

After `docker-compose up -d` completes, follow these steps to get the application ready.

### 1. Open the Application

Navigate to **https://localhost** in your browser.

> The default setup uses a self-signed TLS certificate. Your browser will show a security warning — click "Advanced" → "Proceed" to continue. See [Custom TLS Certificate](#custom-tls-certificate) to use a real certificate.

### 2. Create the Platform Admin

Create the first account from the command line and make it a platform admin:

```sh
docker compose exec gripello gripello admin create-user \
    --email admin@example.com --password 'a-long-password' \
    --username admin --verified --platform-admin
```

Sign in at `https://localhost/auth/login`. Gyms, users and operator settings
(mail, sign-in providers, backups, logs) are managed under `/platform`.

### 3. Create a Gym

Open **Platform → Gyms**, create a gym and invite its staff from the gym's
member settings.

### 4. Configure Email

Without SMTP the app sends no mail at all — a user created in the UI never gets
their invitation and cannot sign in, and the DSA Art. 16 notices are not
delivered. Configure it under **Platform → Mail**, or set these in
`docker-compose.yml` (the platform settings win once a host is saved there):

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Variable
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Purpose
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        SMTP_HOST
      </code>
      
       / <code>
        SMTP_PORT
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Mail server. Setting the host enables SMTP.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        SMTP_USERNAME
      </code>
      
       / <code>
        SMTP_PASSWORD
      </code>
    </td>

      Credentials, if the server needs them.
    </td>
  </tr>

    <td>
      <code>

      </code>
    </td>

        false
      </code>
      
       for STARTTLS; anything else enforces TLS.
    </td>
  </tr>

    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### 5. Configure Application Settings

Go to **Admin → Settings** in the Gripello UI to configure:

- Organisation name and logo
- Privacy policy / imprint URL
- Sign image for route cards
- Grading scale for routes (UIAA, French, YDS) and boulders (Fontainebleau, V-Scale)

### 6. Start Adding Routes

Once signed in as gym staff, use the dashboard to add and manage climbing routes.

## Custom TLS Certificate

By default, a self-signed certificate is generated automatically at startup. To use your own certificate (e.g. from Let's Encrypt), mount it into the container:

```yaml
volumes:
    - ./storage:/data/storage
    - ./backups:/data/backups
    - ./ssl/cert.pem:/etc/nginx/ssl/cert.pem:ro
    - ./ssl/key.pem:/etc/nginx/ssl/key.pem:ro
```

## Rate Limiting

Rate limits are enforced by the container's nginx and need no configuration. They are
sized per client IP for a gym: generous on reads and route ratings, because a
whole hall shares one address behind wifi NAT, and tight on sign-ins and on the
endpoints that send mail. See the `limit_req` zones in `.docker/nginx.conf` for
each rule. `RATE_LIMITS: 'off'` disables them.

The container only believes `X-Forwarded-For` from the addresses in
`TRUSTED_PROXIES` (default `127.0.0.1 ::1`). If you put another reverse proxy in
front of it, make sure that proxy sets `X-Forwarded-For` and list its address or
network, e.g. `TRUSTED_PROXIES: "172.18.0.0/16"`. Without it every visitor is
bucketed as one client and the limits will start rejecting legitimate traffic.
Never list networks that untrusted clients connect from: they could then pick
their own IP and step around the limits.

## Captcha (optional)

Set `CAP_SECRET` to a long random string to require a solved
[Cap](https://trycap.dev) proof-of-work challenge on the actions an anonymous
visitor can trigger: creating a rating, filing a DSA notice, signing in, and the
public password-reset form. Leave it unset and the captcha is simply off — every
form keeps working, which is what an existing install gets after an upgrade.

The puzzle solves itself during submit (about a second on a phone); there is no
checkbox to tick, and the challenge is issued and verified entirely by this
application. Signed-in staff are never asked.

> **Note:** the solver's WebAssembly module is fetched from `cdn.jsdelivr.net`
> at runtime by the upstream widget. Visitors' browsers therefore contact that
> CDN, and the captcha degrades (or fails) on a network that cannot reach it.
> Self-hosting that asset is possible via `window.CAP_CUSTOM_WASM_URL` and is
> not yet wired up here.

Turning it on also raises the two rate limits the captcha now backs, since each
submission costs the client real work.

## Stopping the Service

```sh
docker-compose down
```

Data is persisted in the `postgres` volume, `./storage` and `./backups`, and survives restarts.
